memberdef.definition: typedef int(*) NDXLVertexDynamics(NDXLVertex *_Vertex, double *_dY, const double *_Y, double _Time, void *_Params)
memberdef.name: NDXLVertexDynamics

detaileddescription.para: Defines a user-supplied function that governs how the state of a vertex evolves over time.

parameterdescription.para: Flat output vector containing the time derivative of the calling vertex. ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) total elements must be written to it, even if those elements are zero.
Flat input vector containing the current Runge-Kutta stage of the calling vertex. Is guaranteed to have ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) elements.

Local simulation time of the calling vertex, offset by a fraction of the step size corresponding to the next Runge-Kutta stage. Note that this is generally NOT equivalent to ndxlGetVertexTime(calling_vertex), which only updates on a successful step.
User-defined parameters associated with the calling vertex.

simplesect.para: Integer indicating function success (zero) or failure (any nonzero value).
If this function returns a nonzero value during simulation, NDXL terminates the simulation, and internally raises a NDXL_SIM_ERR.

The function does not verify the number of elements written to the output array. Not writing to each element can result in garbage values or stale states being propagated. Writing beyond ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) elements can result in out-of-bounds writes and undefined behaviour.

memberdef.definition: typedef int(*) NDXLVertexNoise(NDXLVertex *_Vertex, double *_dG, const double *_Y, double _Time, void *_Params)
memberdef.name: NDXLVertexNoise

detaileddescription.para: Defines a user-supplied function that provides the amplitude of noise, for each element in its state vector, for each independent Wiener process the vertex is driven by.

parameterdescription.para: Flat output matrix containing the noise amplitudes, where element ij (at index i * ndxlGetVertexChannelCount(calling_vertex) + j) represents the amplitude of the j-th Wiener process on the i-th state-vector element. ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) x ndxlGetVertexChannelCount(calling_vertex) total elements must be written to it, even if those elements are zero.
Flat input vector containing the current Runge-Kutta stage of the calling vertex. Is guaranteed to have ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) elements.

Local simulation time of the calling vertex, offset by a fraction of the step size corresponding to the next Runge-Kutta stage. Note that this is generally NOT equivalent to ndxlGetVertexTime(calling_vertex), which only updates on a successful step.
User-defined parameters associated with the calling vertex.

simplesect.para: Integer indicating function success (zero) or failure (any nonzero value).
If this function returns a nonzero value during simulation, NDXL terminates the simulation, and internally raises a NDXL_SIM_ERR.

The function does not verify the number of elements written to the output array. Not writing to each element can result in garbage values or stale states being propagated. Writing beyond ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) x ndxlGetVertexChannelCount(calling_vertex) elements can result in out-of-bounds writes and undefined behaviour.

memberdef.definition: typedef int(*) NDXLVertexCallback(NDXLVertex *_Vertex, double *_Y, double _Time, void *_Params)
memberdef.name: NDXLVertexCallback

detaileddescription.para: Defines a user-supplied discrete callback that is invoked during simulation of the vertex's host network.

parameterdescription.para: Flat vector containing the most recently accepted state vector of the calling vertex. Is guaranteed to have ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) elements, and may be modified in-place.
Current simulation time of the calling vertex, equivalent to ndxlGetVertexTime(calling_vertex).
User-defined parameters associated with the calling vertex.

simplesect.para: Integer indicating function success (zero) or failure (any nonzero value).
If this function returns a nonzero value during simulation, NDXL terminates the simulation, and internally raises a NDXL_SIM_ERR.
Writing beyond ndxlGetVertexOrder(calling_vertex) elements to the state vector can result in out-of-bounds writes and undefined behaviour.

briefdescription.para: Dynamics, noise, and callback functions for vertex objects.
